newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian trade sees London coffee taking a breather.
newsitem.headline: Asian trade sees London coffee taking a breather.

text.p: London robusta futures are likely to open slightly lower on Thursday, but any piece of news could spark another explosive rally in the market, Asian coffee dealers said.
"I think London will be US$20 below," a senior dealer for a commodity house told Reuters. "The problem is you're coming into the (frost) season in Brazil"
"If some news comes out that roasters are switching from arabicas to say robustas from the Ivory Coast, the robusta market can go boom," another trader said.
One veteran coffee dealer said he felt the market needed a breather.
"London should be $10 down. I can't see it moving up. But if New York hits $3 (a lb), alarm bells will start ringing," he said.
But other dealers said the London market was still way behind New York. "I think London, compared to New York, is very undervalued," one said. "London has plenty of room to catch up."

The July robusta contract in London closed on Wednesday $53 up on the day after hitting a year peak in early trade of $1,885 a tonne. New York's July contract finished at 240.60 U.S. cents a lb after hitting a lifetime high of 248.50 cents/lb.
Traders said the ability of roasters to switch from expensive arabicas to robustas would be limited.
"It will be very difficult for them to do that. The taste will be so much different," a dealer said.
One dealer said some Indonesian suppliers were beginning to complain that supplies were tight.
Indonesia's benchmark Grade 4 coffee, 80 defects, was quoted by the trade at $1,620/25 a tonne FOB Lampung.
